rendered: The document does not report a sensitivity (limit of detection or similar) for detecting S. typhimurium in human serum. The serum work is a discrimination study, not a detection-limit study. In the serum experiments, bacteria were spiked into human serum and the strains were classified by LDA. The text says the work was done this way: "was investigated in multiple human serum matrix"[1], and the clusters were well classified with almost no overlap. The only limit-of-detection values given are for aqueous samples: P. aeruginosa had an LOD of OD600 =0.0034[2] (CD). S. typhimurium is not given an LOD in either aqueous solution or serum. In aqueous samples it reached only partial discrimination: was achieved for S. typhimurium and S. aureus[3]. So no sensitivity figure for S. typhimurium in human serum can be given from this document.
